subjects.name: Crack epidemic in the United States

summary: Five-part series on how the 1980s US crack epidemic intersected with CIA-tolerated Contra cocaine smuggling, the Iran-Contra arms scheme run by Oliver North, a racialized media panic and harsh sentencing, and the 1996 discrediting of journalist Gary Webb.

evidence.note: crack reaches US inner cities in 1981, starting in southern California
1981 CIA cable warns that new Contra allies ran a trial cocaine flight to Miami
Webb's Dark Alliance series appears in August 1996
CIA inspector general findings on Contra drug ties, the latest period covered at length
small crack-baby study inflated by the press into a moral panic over Black mothers
100-to-1 crack sentencing rule as racist policy driving Black incarceration
housing discrimination, job loss and welfare rules that hit Black inner cities before crack
CIA drug-funding history: Marseille heroin docks, then Golden Triangle opium
Beirut Marine barracks bombing and Hezbollah hostages in Lebanon
North-controlled hangar at Ilopango, El Salvador, used by a Contra pilot moving cocaine
Noriega's Panama drug network and his offer to sabotage Nicaragua for North
McFarlane and North fly to Tehran in 1986 to negotiate directly

notes: Parts 3-4 are Prop's Hood Politics crossover, but formats.yaml lists Cracktoberfest as deep-dive. Roles empty: primary is an event. covered_span ends with the CIA IG review (1998); Webb's 2004 suicide is a short coda (p5 00:49:49). 0.3.0 re-pick: moral-panics and racism replace weapons-arms-trade and policing-incarceration; war-war-crimes also has real time. Coca/CIA heroin history (1855-1970s) under 5% of airtime.
